newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends with small gains after quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends with small gains after quiet trade.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended with tiny gains on Friday in lackluster trading, CBOT floor traders said.
"It was another really quiet day," said a pit trader.

Interest in rice futures this week has been dull because most in the cash trade are attending a rice millers' convention in San Diego. The meeting wraps up this week, so volume is expected to increase next week, traders said.
"Business will pick up next week," said one analyst.
Several factors should spur a larger-than-normal interest in rice futures this summer, traders said.
Dry weather generated by an active El Nino weather pattern could cut into Asian rice production and heavy spring rains have reduced U.S. acreage, one analyst said.
"Interest will be up this summer," said the analyst. "I don't anticipate us working a whole lot lower from here."
Rice closed one to three cents per cwt higher, with July up one at $11.48 per cwt.
Rice futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 200 contracts, below the 85 traded Thursday.
